compatibility.relation_to_k3: typed research extension; no redefinition of canonical K3 arithmetic

claims.statement: A state is a tuple (U,A,M,K,R) of a potential carrier and active, memory, knowledge, and trace projections.

assumptions: U is a set of potential object identifiers
A, M, K, and R are subsets of U

claims.statement: Erase, forget, and deactivate are distinct typed state transformations acting on M, K, and A respectively.

assumptions: The selected object belongs to U

claims.statement: A typed Omega boundary consists of left and right domains together with an interface relation rho included in L times R.

assumptions: L and R are declared sets

claims.statement: Lambda is a vertex in the vertex carrier V of a specified graph G=(V,E).

assumptions: A graph G=(V,E) is fixed

claims.statement: The black-triangle operator is a typed right projection on Omega-boundary expressions: cut(Join(l,r))=r.

scope.domain: Cut expressions over fixed L and R
assumptions: Join is a well-typed constructor

claims.statement: A standard integral is specified by a measure space, a measurable integrand, and integrability conditions.

assumptions: A measure space (X,A,mu) is fixed

claims.statement: A semigroup is a set with an associative binary operation; a two-sided zero absorbs every element on both sides.

assumptions: A binary operation on S is defined

claims.statement: For finite random variables, Shannon entropy and mutual information are defined from the specified probability distribution.

assumptions: Joint probability distribution is specified

claims.statement: A closure operator on P(X) is extensive, monotone, and idempotent; its crystallized states are its fixed points.

assumptions: X is a set

claims.statement: A formal theory is a language, a set of axioms, and a specified derivability relation.

assumptions: A formal language and inference system are fixed

claims.statement: Self-application is defined only for a coded operator and a specified partial application function on codes.

assumptions: A code set and partial application function are fixed

claims.statement: Omega-infinity is a relative set of operator codes whose terminating self-application returns a string outside the chosen theory-code language.

scope.domain: Fixed language L and partial application app
assumptions: C_op and C_Th(L) are fixed

claims.statement: If a semigroup has a left zero l and a right zero r, then l=r.

scope.domain: Any set with a binary operation
assumptions: l*x=l for every x
x*r=r for every x

claims.proof_reference: Section 7.2: evaluate l star r using both absorption laws.

claims.statement: Erasing x from the memory projection does not remove x from the active projection when all unspecified state components are preserved.

assumptions: erase changes M only
x belongs to A before the transition

claims.proof_reference: Section 3.4: the active component is unchanged by definition of erase.

claims.statement: The defined Omega cut operator returns the right component of each well-typed Join expression.

assumptions: Expression is Join_Omega(l,r)

claims.proof_reference: Section 4.3: defining reduction rule for the right projection.

claims.statement: There exists a universal encoding-independent absolute self-application boundary corresponding to the informal item 666 formulation.

assumptions: A nontrivial universal notion of representability must be defined

claims.statement: Give Omega_empty a precise interpretation without identifying it with the empty set or bottom constant.

assumptions: Omega_empty remains a distinct boundary constant

claims.statement: Prove compatibility or exhibit countermodels for the v1, v2, and v3 semantics.

assumptions: Each version is independently typed

claims.statement: Resolve the legacy use of Omega as an integration domain in K3-TI against Omega as a boundary symbol in K3-Omega.

assumptions: Existing K3-TI documents are not silently rewritten

claims.statement: Complete the title, type, definition, dependencies, model, and evidence status for every position in the 666-entry catalogue.

assumptions: Unspecified entries remain visibly incomplete

claims.statement: Choose a proof assistant and establish a reproducible machine-checked correspondence only after the formal kernel and libraries are specified.

assumptions: No proof assistant is currently declared as adopted
